# Decisions

A decision page explains why `claudetto` works the way it does.
Each topic has a heading, the choice, the reason, and a link to the evidence.
Read these pages before you change a part, so that you do not break a fact that a test cannot see.

## Where to Find a Topic

| Topic | Page |
| --- | --- |
| Why the code is split in slices, why files are generated, why bounds have three tiers | [Architecture](Decisions-Architecture) |
| Where plugins live, what each add-on is for | [Layout](Decisions-Layout) |
| The system prompt, the cuts, the request capture, the size of a result | [Prompt](Decisions-Prompt) |
| Settings, off switches, the model choice, when to ask the user | [Settings](Decisions-Settings) |
| Status line, library docs, evals, code graph, Jev | [Tools](Decisions-Tools) |
| Facts of the Claude Code engine | [Engine Facts](Decisions-Engine) |
| What a session costs | [Session Facts](Decisions-Session) |
| Facts from the host, not from the model | [Evidence](Decisions-Evidence) |

[Design](Design) lists the principles that all of these decisions follow.
